entry.content:

News coverage of the Grand Theft Auto franchise since 2001 maps shifting American cultural anxieties and priorities. Early reports on Grand Theft Auto III and Vice City centered on moral panics regarding violence and youth behavior. entry.title: Miguel Dorta Details Custom Game Engine for Satelital
entry.content:
Links: spectralorbit.com | lobsters

Solo developer Miguel Dorta details the seven-year development process behind Satelital, a rule-discovery puzzle game for which he built a custom game engine from scratch. Motivated by a desire to understand the technological fundamentals of video games, Dorta designed his own platform layer, renderer, tools, and editors rather than relying on existing commercial solutions.

Over the course of development, the engine evolved from early iterations using SDL2 and OpenGL to a Vulkan-based backend and a custom base library that replaced parts of the C++ standard library to improve compile times. To achieve a 3D visual style without loading 3D geometry, Dorta utilized orthographic top-down rendering with pre-rendered assets, height maps, and ray-marching shaders for dynamic lighting and shadows.

entry.title: Rockstar Games Details Grand Theft Auto VI Technical Specifications and Resolution Scaling
entry.content:
Links: wccftech.com | r/Games

Rockstar Games has outlined the technical specifications and rendering methods for Grand Theft Auto VI across current-generation consoles, targeting 30 frames per second to support the game's scale and simulation ambitions. On the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, the title upscales a 1440p base resolution to 4K using an in-house temporal anti-aliasing solution, whereas the PlayStation 5 Pro utilizes PSSR2 from a similar 1440p base.

For the Xbox Series S, the game employs AMD FSR 4 upscaling to scale a 720p base resolution to 1080p while successfully implementing ray-traced global illumination despite memory constraints. Developers also addressed artistic choices, confirming that the game's vignette effect is intentional and lacks a toggle, though a bug causing it to intensify improperly in certain circumstances has been fixed.

entry.title: Rockstar Games Details Romance Mechanics and Worldbuilding in Grand Theft Auto VI
entry.content:

In an interview with The Verge, Rockstar North co-studio head and Grand Theft Auto VI producer Rob Nelson discussed the creative and technical choices behind the upcoming open-world game, highlighting a shift toward a romantic central relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia. Nelson acknowledged that building a sustained, interactive romance—complete with joint activities like holding hands and sharing coffee—is a risk for the traditionally chaotic series, though players can choose to bypass these mechanics.

Development on the title began around 2015 with location scouting in Florida to shape the fictional setting of Leonida and Vice City, driving a narrative about small-time criminals rising through the underworld ranks. Building upon the environmental interaction systems of Red Dead Redemption 2, the team incorporated intricate details such as functional bedsheets and synchronized character animations, carefully balancing immersive realism with the franchise's signature fast-paced action.
